title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page Templates
author: Morgan Reyes
body:
Overview
This playbook is the canonical Redwood reference for on-call and incident response. It covers severity taxonomy, the incident lifecycle, role responsibilities, runbooks for common failure modes, the postmortem workflow and template, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and standardized status page and customer communications. Keep this page up to date when runbooks, thresholds, or communication channels change.

Audience
- Engineering on-call responders (SREs and service owners)
- Incident commanders and communications leads
- Customer Success and Support for customer-facing updates

Severity levels and quick guidance
- Sev1 (Critical): Total outage or data integrity loss affecting a large portion of customers or violating contractual SLAs. Immediate page, IC appointed, status page update within 30 minutes.
- Sev2 (High): Major degradation of core functionality (e.g., inference errors or sustained high latency) impacting many customers. Page and urgent response; status updates every 30	60 minutes.
- Sev3 (Medium): Single-customer impact or degraded non-critical feature. Triage during shift and schedule remediation.
- Sev4 (Low): Informational events, noisy alerts, or enhancement work; file ticket.

Incident lifecycle (detailed)
1) Detection & Notification  - Monitoring sources: Prometheus Alertmanager, Grafana synthetic checks, logs anomaly detection, CI deploy events, PagerDuty, support reports.
  - Alert payloads must contain affected service, metrics snapshot, dashboard links, and recent deploy id if available.
2) Acknowledge & Triage (0	610 minutes)  - First responder acknowledges the incident and runs the triage checklist: check recent deploys, config changes, autoscaler events, and cloud provider status.
  - For Sev1/Sev2 the triage owner appoints an Incident Commander (IC) and a Communications lead.
3) Containment & Short-term Mitigation (10	660 minutes)  - IC coordinates mitigations to limit blast radius: traffic reroutes, circuit breakers, model fallbacks, autoscaler adjustments, or temporary rate limits.
  - Publish initial public status update if customers may be affected.
4) Remediation & Recovery  - Execute targeted runbook steps, perform safe rollbacks, and validate metrics and traces show recovery.
5) Post-incident Review & Closure  - Open a postmortem for Sev1/Sev2 incidents within 72 hours. Track action items in the Incident Board (Jira). Close incident once follow-ups are assigned and documented.

Roles and responsibilities- Incident Commander (IC): own timeline, coordinate cross-team actions, and validate recovery.- Triage / First responder: acknowledge alert, collect diagnostics, escalate to IC.- Communications lead: craft status page updates, customer emails, and internal Slack summaries.- SMEs: accountable engineers for runtime, model-serving, infra, networking, and database systems.- Postmortem author: IC or primary SME; responsible for publishing and tracking follow-ups.

Escalation & paging policy
- Paging via PagerDuty. Primary on-call: immediate page. If not acknowledged in 5 minutes -> secondary. If still unacknowledged after 15 minutes -> manager escalation and Slack mention in #incident-alerts.
- Emergency contacts and rotations are maintained in the on-call spreadsheet and PagerDuty schedule.

On-call rotation rules and handoffs
- Rotation length: typically one week for engineers; two-week leadership rotations for senior SREs.
- Handoffs: outgoing on-call posts a Handoff note in #oncall with open incidents, suppressed alerts, and temporary mitigations before leaving shift.
- Swap policy: use PagerDuty swap flow and notify rotation owner; for prolonged absences coordinate a replacement two weeks in advance.

Runbooks (excerpts)
API latency spike (quick checklist)- Symptom: sustained p95 > 300ms for >5 minutes.- Immediate checks: confirm Grafana alert, check recent deploys and canary metrics, inspect traces for slow spans, check worker queues and autoscaler.- Mitigations (priority): revert recent deploy; increase min replicas; enable model quantized fallback or route traffic to dedicated pools; apply temporary rate limits for non-critical routes.- Validation: p95 returns to target for 10 consecutive minutes before close.

GPU worker OOM or model load failures- Symptom: CrashLoopBackOff, CUDA OOM, model load errors.- Steps: identify affected pods (kubectl get pods -n runtime); view previous logs; check GPU memory metrics; drain and reschedule pod to node with sufficient memory or switch model variant; scale node pool if necessary.- Post-incident: file quantization profile/auto-scaling tuning task.

Postgres connection or latency issues- Symptom: connection errors, increased DB latency, query timeouts.- Steps: check DB cluster health, failover events, connection pool saturation; tune application pool sizes or enable pooling proxy; if provider incident, failover to replica or enable read-only modes where applicable.

Game days and exercises
- Cadence: minimum quarterly runbooks testing per team; at least one company-wide production game day every six months.
- Goals: validate runbooks, test cross-team coordination, measure MTTA/MTTR, and rehearse customer comms.
- After action: publish exercise postmortem, list actions with owners and due dates.

Postmortem workflow & template
- Deadlines: draft postmortem within 72 hours; stakeholder review within 7 days; final publish with owners assigned.
- Template fields: title, incident id, severity, start/end times, impact summary, timeline of events, root cause, contributing factors, mitigations and long-term remediations, action items (owner + due date), and lessons learned.

Status page and customer communication patterns
- Update cadence: for Sev1/Sev2 post updates every 30	60 minutes or when there is a material change. Use clear, non-technical language for customer messages and a more detailed internal channel for engineers.
- Use the following templates:
Initial public message:
  Title: [Incident] Redwood API 	6 Degraded Performance
  Body: We are investigating elevated error rates and increased latency in inference for customers in us-west. Engineers are actively triaging. We will provide updates every 30 minutes.
Progress update:
  Title: [Update] Redwood API 	6 Partial Recovery
  Body: Engineering identified a routing configuration that increased load on a subset of inference pools. A mitigation has been applied and we are seeing reduced errors. Some clients may still experience degraded performance; ETA for full resolution: ~45 minutes.
Resolution message:
  Title: [Resolved] Redwood API 	6 Service Restored
  Body: The issue is resolved. Root cause: routing configuration change deployed to canary that incorrectly rolled out to additional pools. We reverted the change and validated traffic distribution. A postmortem will be published.

Internal incident channel example
- IC: @morgan.reyes
- Severity: Sev1
- Impact: Inference latency & 5xx errors, ~18% of traffic affected
- Actions taken: rolled backed deploy, scaled dedicated inference pool, opened ticket with cloud provider.
- Next steps: draft postmortem, schedule stakeholder review.

Communications best practices
- Be transparent, concise, and factual. Do not speculate about root cause in initial updates. Align external messaging with Customer Success for enterprise SLA cases.

Monitoring & diagnostics checklist
- Key dashboards: API availability, latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, token generation success, GPU utilization, queue lengths.- Logs & traces: correlate request IDs, inspect slow spans, and search for OOMs or resource errors.

Post-incident tracking and verification
- Track follow-ups in the Incident Board (Jira) with owners and due dates. IC verifies completion of action items and marks incident follow-ups as done.

References & links
- Runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- PagerDuty schedules: (PagerDuty link)
- Status page: (status.redwood.example)

Quick commands
- List runtime pods: kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide
- Tail logs: kubectl logs -n runtime <pod> --follow
- Check HPA: kubectl get hpa -n runtime

Ownership and contact
- On-call rotation owner: eng-sre rota manager (eng-sre@redwood.example)
- Incident review board: Eng leadership, Product, Customer Success for Sev1 reviews.

Feedback and continuous improvement
- If runbooks lack clarity or alerts are noisy, file an item in the Oncall Improvements epic and tag the eng-sre rotation owner. Regularly review runbook accuracy after game days and incidents.
